items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Earl wanted him to come to Chicago and to be with the band. So, he did... Arthur Lee's singing in the band

ctx.x: The transportation was easy, and I never will forget. We had been down on one of our tours with Earl to Augusta, Georgia. And, we met this young man by the name of Arthur Lee Simpkins. And, we pursuaded him -- he was a good singer. So, we -- Earl wanted him to come to Chicago and to be with the band. So, he did.

We called him Georgia boy. And -- but, he was very intelligent. And, could sing. His name was Arthur Lee Simpkins. And, I never will forget one night. We're in there and Arthur Lee's singing in the band, and there's just -- all of a sudden this voice came out like from nowhere. 'There's my nigger.' And, when he said that, well, Bowman was the head waiter. And, these waiters went over and grabbed this cat and was really walking him. They were beating the hell out this man.
